items.name: Jocote
items.desc: Jocotes are small oval fruits, about the size of a grape tomato to a small plum, with a slightly elongated teardrop shape and often a small knob at the tip. The skin is thin, smooth, and glossy with no dusty bloom, and a pile shows the whole ripening range: some fruit yellow-green, most orange-red to deep red, a few nearly purple, with occasional light brown scuffs. There is no visible stem or leaf. They are sold loose by the pound, shown as a small heap of about fifteen fruit sitting fully inside the frame with every fruit whole and visible.

items.name: Lulo
items.desc: A lulo is a round fruit about the size of a small tomato, with a thick, leathery, bright golden-orange skin that is smooth to faintly velvety, with a trace of fine brown fuzz near the top. The stem end is capped by a stiff, rough, five-pointed greenish-brown calyx with a short dry stalk. The body is evenly round without ribs or shoulders and the color is uniform golden orange with no green patches. It is sold whole and loose by the pound, shown as a single whole fruit, never cut.

items.name: Chilacayota
items.desc: A chilacayota is a large, clearly elongated oblong squash, about twice as long as it is wide, with bluntly rounded ends, lying on its side. The rind is hard, smooth, and faintly glossy, mid-to-dark green and irregularly mottled with cream-white blotches, speckles, and short broken streaks of uneven size and shape, never even stripes and never star-shaped spots. A short, hard, ridged tan stem sits at one end. The surface has no ribs. It is sold whole by the pound, shown as a single squash.

items.name: Huauzontle
items.desc: Huauzontle is sold as a bunch of long, slender, upright green branches, each thickly covered along its upper length with dense clusters of tiny unopened green flower buds that form narrow, bumpy, feathery spikes. The stems are thin and wiry, faintly tinged with red near the base, and carry only a few small diamond-shaped green leaves between the bud clusters, so the bunch reads as bud-covered stalks rather than a leafy green. The buds are fine and granular, soft yellow-green to mid green, with no domed heads and no open flowers. It is a bunch of several forearm-length branches tied together at the stem ends.

items.name: Guajes
items.desc: Guajes are long, flat, strap-like green pods, about 20 to 28 centimeters long and 2 to 3 centimeters wide, straight or very gently curved, tapering to a short point at each end. The surface is smooth and matte, pale to light green, often finely speckled, and one face commonly shows a reddish-brown blush. A single row of flat oval seeds shows through the pod as a line of gentle bumps along its length. They are sold fresh as a cluster of several pods fanning out from one shared stalk.

items.name: Alache
items.desc: Alache is sold as a loose bunch of tender, slender, ridged green stems carrying alternate, long-stalked leaves. The leaves are medium green, matte and softly hairy, roughly triangular to arrowhead-shaped with a pointed tip, often showing three shallow lobes and a coarsely toothed edge, and many carry a faint dark purple streak along the midvein. Leaves are about 4 to 8 centimeters long. A few small five-petaled lavender-purple flowers on long stalks appear among the leaves. It is a bunch of several stems gathered at the base.

items.name: Culantro
items.desc: Culantro leaves are long, flat, and lance-shaped, about 15 to 25 centimeters long and 3 to 5 centimeters wide, glossy dark green with a pale central midrib and a finely saw-toothed edge along the entire margin, each small tooth ending in a tiny pale spine. The leaves are thick and leathery and grow directly from a short crown with no stalks, fanning out from a single base like a loose rosette. It is sold as a small bunch of roughly eight to twelve whole leaves held together by a band near the base, the leaves spreading upward and outward, sometimes with a short pale taproot still attached.

items.name: Chile de Árbol, Fresh
items.desc: Fresh chile de arbol pods are long, slender, and cylindrical, about 5 to 8 centimeters long and only a centimeter wide, tapering evenly to a fine sharp point and often bending slightly along their length. The skin is smooth, glossy, and taut, most pods a deep green with a few in the pile turning orange or bright red, and each pod carries a long, thin green stem that curves away from the small green cap. The flesh is thin and the pods look light and pliable rather than plump. They are sold loose by the pound, shown as a small heap of about twenty pods sitting fully inside the frame with every pod whole and visible, their stems tangling together.

items.name: Chile Manzano
items.desc: Chile manzano is a small, round, apple-shaped pepper about 3 to 5 centimeters across, with a smooth, taut, waxy skin in a uniform golden yellow to yellow-orange. The body is plump and gently lobed, with a shallow dimple at the top where a long, slender green stem bends away from a small green calyx, and a smoothly rounded base with no point. The walls are thick and the pod looks solid and heavy for its size. It is sold loose as whole pods, shown as a small pile of several whole pods, one of them halved to reveal the thick flesh around a cavity of small flat black seeds.

items.name: Bolillo Roll
items.desc: A bolillo is a Mexican crusty white bread roll about six inches long, shaped like a short torpedo: plump in the middle and tapering to two blunt points at the ends. One single long score runs lengthwise down the top and bursts open in the oven into a raised ridge that shows a paler cream-colored edge. The crust is thin, crisp, and golden brown with a faint sheen, and the underside is paler and lightly floury. It is much shorter than a baguette and carries only one slash, and it is not a telera, which is flatter and rounder with two parallel grooves across the top. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Glazed Donut
items.desc: A glazed donut is the plain, regular donut of the bakery case: one round yeast-raised ring with a clean hole in the center, soft and puffy, golden brown on top and bottom with a pale cream-colored band around its outer side where it floated in the fryer. The whole top and sides are coated in a thin, translucent, shiny sugar glaze with a faint crackled sheen, with no sprinkles, no colored frosting, and no filling. It is a fried bakery item, not the flat donut peach or saturn peach of the produce aisle. It is sold by the each, shown as a single whole donut from a three-quarter top view with the hole clearly visible.

items.name: Muffin
items.desc: A bakery muffin is a single tall quick-bread pastry baked in a pleated white paper liner, with a large golden-brown domed top that rises and spills slightly over the edge of the liner. The crust is rough, craggy, and crackled, dotted with dark purple-blue blueberries bursting at the surface and a light scatter of coarse sparkling sugar. It has no frosting, which sets it apart from a cupcake. It is sold by the each from the bakery pastry case, shown as a single whole blueberry muffin from a slight three-quarter side view so both the liner and the dome are visible.

items.name: Concha (Pan Dulce)
items.desc: A concha is the best-known Mexican pan dulce: a round, domed, palm-sized soft sweet bun whose top is covered by a thick, crumbly sugar-paste topping scored into a seashell pattern, curved grooves fanning out like a scallop shell. The classic vanilla concha has a pale cream-white topping, with the golden-brown bread showing through the cracks between the topping sections and a golden-brown bun base around the lower edge; pink and chocolate toppings are also common. The shell pattern sets it apart from other pan dulce such as cuernos or orejas. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole vanilla concha from a three-quarter top view.

items.name: Flour Tortillas
items.desc: Flour tortillas are thin, round, soft flatbreads made from wheat flour, pale cream to off-white with scattered light golden-brown toasted spots from the griddle, soft and pliable with slightly uneven round edges. They are paler, thinner, and larger than corn tortillas, which are yellow and thicker. They are sold by the stack, often fresh from the store's tortilleria, shown as a neat small pile of about six tortillas lying flat from a three-quarter top view.

items.name: Green Almonds
items.desc: Green almonds are small, flattened oval fruits about the size of a large grape, each shaped like a plump almond with one end slightly more pointed than the other and a faint seam along one edge. The hull is pale to mid green and covered all over in soft, velvety fuzz that gives it a matte, faintly silvery sheen, never glossy and never orange or blushed. Some carry a short, thin green-brown stem; there are no leaves and no hard tan shell. They are flatter and more pointed than apricots or green plums and much shorter than bean pods. They are sold loose by the pound in spring, shown as a small pile of about twelve green almonds sitting fully inside the frame with every almond whole and visible.

items.name: Green Pistachios
items.desc: Fresh pistachios are small teardrop-shaped fruits about the size of a large chickpea to a small olive, each fuller at one end and tapering to a soft point. The soft, smooth, matte hull is pale cream to yellow-green, blushed in patches with rose pink, red and dusky purple-red, often with a few tiny pale speckles or small light-brown bruises, so a heap shows a mix of creamy and rosy fruit rather than one solid color. The hull covers the whole fruit; no beige shell and no green nut show, and the fruit is opaque, not glassy like a grape. A few fruits are still joined on short, thin, branching tan-green stems. They are sold loose by the pound in late summer, shown as a small pile of about fifteen fresh pistachios sitting fully inside the frame with every pistachio whole and visible.

items.name: Green Olives
items.desc: Fresh green olives are firm, smooth, evenly oval fruits about the size of a large grape, symmetrical with gently rounded ends, a tiny stem scar at one end, and no point or beak. The skin is taut and glossy with a light waxy shine, an even bright leaf green to slightly yellowish green, with a few tiny pale dots, and one or two olives in the pile are just turning, blushed violet-purple at one end, never red or orange. They are opaque and solid-looking, never translucent like grapes, never veined like gooseberries, and never wrinkled, cracked, or wet like brined olives. There are no leaves and no stems. They are sold loose by the pound in fall for home curing, shown as a small pile of about twenty olives sitting fully inside the frame with every olive whole and visible.

items.name: Grape Leaves
items.desc: Fresh grape leaves are thin, flat, hand-sized leaves with a broad, roughly heart-shaped outline, three to five shallow pointed lobes, a deep notch where the short leaf stem joins, and finely toothed edges all the way around. The top surface is smooth, slightly satiny, bright to mid green, with fine pale veins fanning out from the stem point; the underside is a paler gray-green. They are broad and lobed, never the narrow smooth-edged oval of a bay leaf, and thinner, smoother and more finely toothed than a fig leaf, with no grapes or tendrils. They are sold by the pound in late spring and early summer, shown as a neat stacked pile of about ten fresh grape leaves lying flat, the top leaf fully visible and the edges of the leaves beneath fanned out slightly, with their short stems together at the bottom, all fully inside the frame.

items.name: Molokhia (Jute Mallow)
items.desc: Mloukhiye is sold as a bunch of long, slender, leafy stems, the stems green with a faint reddish-brown tint, each carrying many glossy dark green leaves set one at a time alternately along its length on short thin leaf stalks. The leaves are flat and thin, narrowly oval to lance-shaped, about 5 to 10 centimeters long, tapering to a pointed tip, with a finely saw-toothed edge, a pale midrib, and prominent veins. At the base of each leaf the two lowest teeth stretch into a pair of fine thread-like bristles that curve back toward the stalk, a detail spinach, mint, and basil never show. The leaves are not paired like mint or basil, not broad and smooth-edged like spinach, and carry no flowers. It is a bunch of about ten forearm-length leafy stems tied together at the stem ends, the leaves spreading outward, the whole bunch with every leaf tip and both stem ends sitting fully inside the frame with a small margin all around.

items.name: Kusa Squash
items.desc: Kusa is a short summer squash about 12 to 15 centimeters long and about a third as wide, a straight, smooth cylinder that widens slightly toward the blossom end and has bluntly rounded ends. The skin is thin, smooth, and faintly glossy, a soft pale mint to gray-green with fine, faint whitish speckles, much lighter than a dark green zucchini and clearly green, never cream-white. A short, ridged green stem stub sits at the narrow end and a small dry blossom scar at the other. It is about half the length of a regular zucchini and a little stockier than a baby zucchini, with no ribs or furrows. It is sold loose by the pound, shown as a small pile of about five squash lying side by side, sitting fully inside the frame with every squash whole and visible.

items.name: Garden Cress (Rashad)
items.desc: Rashad is garden cress sold as a bunch of young, tender plants about 25 centimeters tall, with slender, smooth, pale green stems that branch near the top. The leaves are small, about 4 to 8 centimeters long, thin, flat, and matte, a fresh light-to-medium green, mostly spoon-shaped to oblong with finely toothed or shallowly lobed edges, and a few narrow strap-like leaves near the stem tips. The leaves sit singly along the upper stems rather than in round paired leaflets like watercress, and they are smaller, lighter, and far less deeply lobed than arugula. There are no roots, no flowers, and no tray of sprouts. It is a bunch of about twenty slender stems gathered and tied near the cut base, the leaves loosely spreading at the top.

items.name: Turmeric Root
items.desc: Fresh turmeric is sold as small, slender, finger-like rhizomes, each about the length of a thumb or a little longer and much thinner than ginger, slightly curved, with an occasional short knob or side branch. The thin skin is rough, tan-brown with a warm orange cast, and marked with fine, closely spaced rings, with a few spots where bright orange shows through. Beside the whole fingers lies exactly one finger cut crosswise, showing a dense, vivid carrot-orange interior with a slightly lighter orange ring under the skin, which tells it apart from ginger and its pale beige flesh. These are separate small fingers, not one large, plump, branched ginger hand. It is sold loose by the pound, shown as a small pile of about seven fingers plus the one cut finger, sitting fully inside the frame with every piece whole and visible.

items.name: Sour Grapes (Hosrom)
items.desc: Sour hosrom are unripe grapes picked weeks before they sweeten, sold as a small, compact bunch of hard, perfectly round berries on fresh green stems. Each berry is about the size of a large pea to a small marble, clearly smaller and rounder than a ripe green table grape, and the berries sit tightly packed against each other. The skin is smooth and taut, a deep, even grass green to slightly olive green, opaque with only a faint sheen and none of the pale yellow-green, see-through glow of ripe green grapes. The branching stems are pale green and fresh, not brown or woody. They are sold by the pound, shown as a single short bunch of about thirty berries hanging from its stem, sitting fully inside the frame with every berry whole and visible.

items.name: Sour Plums, Green
items.desc: Green sour plums are small, hard, unripe plums about the size of a cherry tomato or a large grape, round to slightly oval, each with a faint seam running down one side. The skin is thin, taut, smooth, and glossy, an even bright emerald to grass green with no yellow, no blush, and no dusty bloom. They are far smaller, shinier, and greener than a ripe green plum or a green plumcot, and each is a separate loose fruit. A few carry a tiny thin green stalk; most have none. They are sold loose by the pound, shown as a small pile of about twelve plums sitting fully inside the frame with every plum whole and visible.

items.name: Cacao Pod
items.desc: A cacao pod is a large, heavy fruit about 20 to 25 cm long and 9 cm wide, shaped like an elongated football: widest just below the middle, tapering to a blunt point at the tip, with a short, thick, woody stem stub at the other end. Ten deep furrows run lengthwise from the stem to the tip, with rounded ridges between them. The husk is thick, hard, leathery and matte, rough and bumpy with small warts along the ridges, never smooth or glossy. The color is a ripe deep red-maroon to red-brown, with orange-red patches on the ridges and orange-yellow showing in the furrows, and a few small dark brown scuffs. It is sold whole by the each, shown as one whole, closed pod, never cut or opened, with no leaves, lying at a slight diagonal and sitting fully inside the frame with both ends visible.

items.name: Baladi Cucumber
items.desc: Baladi cucumbers are short, plump local slicing cucumbers about 12 to 15 cm long and 3 to 4 cm wide, straight to very slightly curved, with blunt rounded ends, a small dry stem scar at one end and a tiny pale blossom spot at the other. The skin is thin and tender with a soft satin sheen, not waxy, a clear leaf green with faint paler green streaks running lengthwise from the blossom end, very shallow lengthwise ridges, and a few tiny pale bumps; no deep furrows, no spines, and no fuzz. They are much shorter and plumper than a long slicing cucumber, and lighter green and less uniform than slim, dark, glossy snacking cucumbers. They are sold loose by the pound, shown as a small group of three whole cucumbers lying side by side at a slight diagonal, fully inside the frame with both ends of each one visible.

items.name: Montreal Bagels
items.desc: Montreal bagels are hand-rolled, wood-fired bagels about 9 cm across, smaller, flatter, and denser than a puffy New York bagel, with a noticeably large center hole about a third of the bagel's width and a slightly uneven hand-rolled ring. The crust is thin, crisp, and glossy, a deep golden to amber brown with a few darker toasted spots from the wood fire, and the top and sides are thickly coated in toasted sesame seeds, cream to golden in color. They are sold loose by the each from the bakery, shown as a group of three whole bagels, two lying flat side by side and one leaning against them, fully inside the frame with every hole clearly visible, uncut, with no spread and no plate.

items.name: Mini Cucumbers
items.desc: Mini cucumbers are small seedless snack cucumbers about 12 to 15 cm long and 3 cm wide, slim and straight with a gentle taper to blunt rounded ends and a small dried stem scar at one end. The skin is thin, smooth and glossy, a dark green with faint lighter green lengthwise stripes, almost no bumps and no spines. They are much shorter and slimmer than a long English cucumber and darker and glossier than a plump Baladi cucumber. They are sold in small bags or trays or loose by the each, shown as three whole cucumbers lying loosely side by side at a slight diagonal, with no packaging, no tray and no leaves or flowers, fully inside the frame with both ends of each one visible.

items.name: Water Gallon Jug
items.desc: A water gallon jug is the plain one-gallon clear plastic jug a store fills with drinking water at its refill station: a squarish clear jug with a built-in carry handle on the shoulder and a white screw cap, slightly translucent, filled with clear water, standing upright. It is shown as one jug, completely blank, with no label, no sticker, no printing, no logo and no brand.

items.name: Bulk Candy
items.desc: Bulk candy is the loose mixed candy a store sells by weight from self-serve bulk bins: a small loose pile of round jelly beans, sugar-coated orange and lemon fruit slices, small round gumdrops and sugared gummy rings in red, orange, yellow, green and purple, heaped on the surface. It is shown with no fish, bear, worm, animal or character shapes, and with no bag, no bin, no scoop, no wrappers, no brand, no text and no labels.

items.name: Empty Bottle Crate
items.desc: An empty bottle crate is the returnable hard-plastic beverage crate a shopper brings back to the store for the deposit: one rectangular blue plastic crate with ribbed side walls, a hand-hold opening on each short side and a molded grid of 20 round bottle compartments inside, shown empty from the front and slightly above. It is shown with no bottles, no caps, no label, no printing, no logo and no brand.

items.name: Soft Pretzel
items.desc: A soft pretzel is the German lye pretzel (Laugenbrezel): one knotted pretzel about 13 cm wide with a thick, plump belly along the bottom and thin arms that cross over each other and loop back to it. The crust is a glossy deep mahogany brown from the lye bath, a pale cream split opens along the thick belly, and coarse white pretzel salt is scattered over the top. It has no cheese, no seeds and no butter filling. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole pretzel.

items.name: Pretzel Stick
items.desc: A pretzel stick is the German lye stick (Laugenstange): one straight bread stick about 22 cm long and 4 cm thick with rounded ends. The crust is a glossy deep chestnut brown from the lye bath, three or four short diagonal slashes on top open into pale cream-white crumb, and coarse white pretzel salt crystals are scattered across the top. It has no cheese and no seeds, and it is straight, not a knotted pretzel or a triangle. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole stick lying diagonally.

items.name: Cheese Pretzel Stick
items.desc: A cheese pretzel stick is the German lye stick topped with baked cheese (Laugenstange mit Käse): one straight stick about 22 cm long and 4.5 cm thick with a glossy dark chestnut-brown lye crust and three diagonal slashes showing pale crumb. A thick strip of grated Gouda is melted and baked along the whole top, golden yellow with toasted light-brown edges and lacy bits running down the sides. It has only a few salt crystals and no seeds. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole stick lying diagonally.

items.name: Seeded Pretzel Stick
items.desc: A seeded pretzel stick is the German lye stick with a seed crust (Laugenstange mit Saaten): one straight stick about 22 cm long and 4.5 cm thick with a glossy dark chestnut-brown lye crust and short diagonal slashes showing pale crumb. The whole top is densely covered in a toasted seed mix of flat green-gray pumpkin seeds, pale gray sunflower kernels, cream sesame and small dark brown flaxseeds. It has no cheese and no coarse salt. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole stick lying diagonally.

items.name: Butter Pretzel Croissant Triangle
items.desc: A butter pretzel croissant triangle is the German Laugen-Butter-Ecke: one flat triangular pastry about 12 cm on each side and 5 cm tall, made of flaky butter croissant dough brushed with pretzel lye. The top is a smooth, glossy, deep reddish-brown pretzel crust, and the cut sides show many thin golden puffed layers like a croissant. It carries at most a few coarse salt crystals, with no seeds and no cheese, and it is the only flaky triangle with a lye-brown top. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole pastry.

items.name: Kaiser Roll
items.desc: A Kaiser roll is the round crusty white roll about 9 cm across stamped on top with five curved segments that swirl out from the center in a pinwheel. The crust is thin, crisp and matte golden brown, a little darker on the ridges of the stamp, with a faint dusting of flour. It has no seeds, no shine and no single lengthwise cut, which sets it apart from the oval split-top roll. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Split-Top Roll
items.desc: A split-top roll is the German wheat roll (Schnittbrötchen, Schrippe): one oval crusty white roll about 11 cm long and 7 cm wide with one deep cut down the middle that has burst open into a raised, rough-edged ridge, paler golden-cream than the rest. The crust is thin, crisp and slightly shiny, an even golden brown with fine blistering. It has no flour dusting, no seeds and no star stamp. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Stone-Oven Roll
items.desc: A stone-oven roll (Steinofenbrötchen) is a rustic squarish wheat roll about 10 cm long, 8 cm wide and 6 cm tall, irregular and slightly flattened like a small ciabatta. The crust is thick and matte, golden to medium brown, heavily dusted with white flour that has cracked into a fine crackle pattern, and an uneven open seam runs along the top where the dough folded and burst, showing coarse airy crumb. It has no seeds and no shine. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Sesame Roll
items.desc: A sesame roll (Sesambrötchen) is a round-to-oval crusty white wheat roll about 10 cm across whose whole top is evenly and thickly coated in hulled cream-white sesame seeds, lightly toasted to a pale gold, so it looks speckled cream and tan. Where the crust shows at the sides it is thin, crisp and golden brown. It carries only sesame, with no black poppy seeds and no sunflower or pumpkin seeds. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Poppy Seed Roll
items.desc: A poppy seed roll (Mohnbrötchen) is an oval crusty white wheat roll about 11 cm long whose whole top is densely coated in tiny blue-black poppy seeds, so it looks almost charcoal gray-black, with one lengthwise cut down the middle that opens into a paler golden ridge free of seeds. The bottom and sides show a thin golden brown crust. It carries only poppy seeds, with no sesame and no sunflower seeds. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Pumpkin Seed Roll
items.desc: A pumpkin seed roll (Kürbiskernbrötchen) is a squarish domed wheat roll about 9 cm across and 6 cm tall whose top is covered with large flat oval pumpkin seeds, dark olive green to toasted brown, overlapping like scales. More green seed pieces show in the light brown, slightly grainy crust on the sides, with a light flour dusting at the base. It carries only pumpkin seeds, with no sunflower kernels, no sesame and no poppy. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Sunflower Seed Roll
items.desc: A sunflower seed roll (Sonnenblumenkernbrötchen) is a round domed wheat roll about 10 cm across whose whole top is thickly crusted with small pale gray-tan sunflower kernels, toasted golden at the tips. The crust beneath is a medium brown, slightly grainy multigrain crust with kernels pressed into the sides. It carries only sunflower kernels, with no green pumpkin seeds, no black poppy and no sesame. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Multi-Seed Roll
items.desc: A multi-seed roll is the German Weltmeister roll (Weltmeisterbrötchen): an oblong rectangular multigrain roll with rounded corners, about 12 cm long, 8 cm wide and 5 cm tall. The whole top is densely coated in a mix of tiny blue-black poppy seeds and pale cream sesame seeds, a salt-and-pepper speckle over a deep golden-brown crust, and sunflower kernels and oat flakes show in the sides. It has no pumpkin seeds and no flour dusting. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Seeded Spelt Roll
items.desc: A seeded spelt roll (Dinkelbrötchen mit Saaten) is an oval roll about 13 cm long and 7 cm wide, tapering slightly at the ends, with a rustic, matte, medium brown crust lightly dusted with white flour that has cracked into fine lines, and one long shallow cut along the top. Seeds are scattered sparsely in and on the crust rather than coating it: green pumpkin seed pieces, golden-brown flaxseeds and a few sunflower kernels. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Rye Roll
items.desc: A rye roll (Roggenbrötchen) is a squarish, slightly flattened roll about 9 cm across and 5 cm tall, the darkest of the bakery rolls. The crust is a dark reddish brown, matte and dull, under a thin layer of white rye flour that has cracked into an irregular network of fine fissures across the top. It has no cuts, no seeds and no shine. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll.

items.name: Butter Croissant
items.desc: A butter croissant (Buttercroissant) is the plain croissant of the bakery case: one plump crescent about 15 cm long, rolled into about seven segments that taper toward the curved ends. The flaky layers are glossy golden amber, a little darker on the ridges, with thin crisp layers showing along the sides. It has no filling, no cheese, no nuts and no topping. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole croissant.

items.name: Ham and Cheese Croissant
items.desc: A ham and cheese croissant (Käse-Schinken-Croissant) is one curved crescent croissant about 16 cm long with a flaky, layered, golden brown body whose top is covered with grated cheese baked into a lacy, bubbly crust of golden yellow and toasted brown spots running over the ridges. A little pink cooked ham peeks out of the rolled ends. It has no chopped nuts, no chocolate and no sugar. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole croissant.

items.name: Hazelnut Chocolate Croissant
items.desc: A hazelnut chocolate croissant (Nuss-Nougat-Croissant) is one plump curved croissant about 16 cm long, flaky, layered and shiny golden brown, filled with chocolate hazelnut cream that shows as a dark brown streak at the rolled ends. The top ridge is sprinkled with chopped roasted hazelnut pieces, light brown and craggy. It has no cheese, no ham and no powdered sugar. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole croissant.

items.name: Baguette
items.desc: A baguette (Weizenbaguette) is the long thin French-style wheat loaf, about 55 cm long and 6 cm wide with rounded ends. The crust is thin, crisp and smooth, an even shiny golden brown, with five or six neat diagonal slashes along the top that open into lighter cream-gold ridges. It has no flour dusting, no seeds and no twist, unlike the floury stone-oven baguette. It is sold by the each, shown as a single whole loaf lying diagonally.

items.name: Stone-Oven Baguette
items.desc: A stone-oven baguette (Steinofenbaguette) is a long rustic loaf about 50 cm long and 7 cm wide, irregular and slightly twisted with pointed, uneven ends. The crust is thick, matte and darker, deep golden to chestnut brown with blistered dark spots, heavily dusted with white flour, and one long ragged burst seam runs along the top showing open airy crumb. It has no neat row of cuts and no seeds. It is sold by the each, shown as a single whole loaf lying diagonally.

items.name: Ciabatta
items.desc: A ciabatta is the Italian-style white loaf of the bake-off counter: one flat, wide, rectangular slipper-shaped loaf about 25 cm long, 12 cm wide and only 5 cm tall, with rounded corners and slightly uneven edges. The crust is thin, pale golden and matte with a heavy dusting of white flour and gentle irregular dimples. It has no slashes, no seeds and no shine, unlike the long thin baguettes. It is sold by the each, shown as a single whole loaf.

items.name: Brioche Knot
items.desc: A brioche knot is a soft sweet yeast bun about 10 cm across and 6 cm tall, made from a rope of rich brioche dough tied into a round knot, with two or three smooth plump strands looping over each other and the end tucked in on top. The surface is very glossy from egg wash, a deep shiny amber to golden brown, darker on the high points, with pale soft creases between the strands. It has no seeds, no salt and no icing. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole knot.

items.name: Jelly Donut
items.desc: A jelly donut is the German Berliner (Berliner Pfannkuchen, Krapfen): a round filled yeast doughnut with no hole, about 9 cm across and 5 cm tall, its domed top and bottom fried golden brown and the top evenly dusted with fine white sugar. A pale cream-white band runs around its middle where it floated in the fat, and the jam filling stays inside, out of sight. It has no glaze, no chocolate and no hole. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole doughnut from the side and slightly above.

items.name: Quark Donut Ball
items.desc: A quark donut ball (Quarkbällchen) is a small round fried doughnut ball about 4.5 cm across, an almost perfect sphere with a slightly uneven medium golden-brown surface, completely rolled in coarse sparkling white granulated sugar that clings all over. It has no visible filling, no hole, no glaze and no pale middle band, and it is about half the size of a Berliner. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole ball.

items.name: Quark Danish
items.desc: A quark Danish (Quarktasche) is a square Danish-style pastry about 11 cm across made of flaky golden butter pastry, its four corners folded in toward the center like an envelope, leaving a small opening where the white-cream sweet quark filling bulges out. The top is shiny with a thin apricot glaze, golden brown with paler layered edges. It has no apple, no icing stripes and no nuts. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole pastry.

items.name: Apple Turnover
items.desc: An apple turnover is the bake-off counter's closed triangular puff-pastry pocket filled with apple, about 12 cm on its long side: flaky and golden brown with thin pastry layers showing along its two sealed edges, and a crust of coarse sparkling sugar crystals over the whole top. The top is closed, with no slits or cut-outs, no white icing or glaze stripes, and no powdered sugar; at most a hint of pale apple filling shows at one sealed corner. It differs from the quark danish, which is a square envelope with white quark showing in the middle. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole turnover.

items.name: Sausage Roll
items.desc: A sausage roll is the German Würstchendog: a whole pink-brown frankfurter wrapped in a spiral of flaky golden laminated pastry, a log about 12 cm long and 4 cm thick, the strip winding around it in overlapping diagonal bands with paler layered edges. One end of the sausage peeks out, reddish brown and glossy, and a little ketchup stays inside, out of sight. It has no seeds, no cheese and no lye crust. It is sold loose by the each, shown as a single whole roll lying diagonally.

items.name: Snack Pizza
items.desc: A snack pizza is the small round single-serving pizza of the bake-off counter, about 13 cm across and flat, with a thin base and a narrow, low golden rim. The top is covered almost to the rim in melted pale mozzarella with golden-brown baked spots, small red pieces of diced tomato scattered across it, and small green flecks of basil. It carries no olives, capers, salami, ham or mushrooms. It is much smaller than a family pizza and is sold whole and uncut, loose by the each, shown as a single pizza seen from above.

items.name: Double Roll
items.desc: A double roll (Doppelschrippe) is one wheat roll about 14 cm long made of two round halves joined at a pinched waist, like a peanut. Each half carries one short lengthwise cut that has burst open into a pale cream ridge, and the crust is thin, crisp and evenly golden brown with a dull finish and no flour. It has no seeds, no salt and no pinwheel pattern, which sets it apart from the Kaiser roll and the single oval split-top roll. Shown as one whole roll with both halves joined; it must show no text and no packaging.

items.name: Pretzel Roll
items.desc: A pretzel roll (Laugenbrötchen) is an oval roll about 10 cm long with the glossy, deep mahogany-brown skin of a pretzel. One deep cut down the middle has burst open into a wide, pale cream-white band that contrasts sharply with the dark crust, and a few coarse white salt crystals sit on top. It is not knotted like a pretzel, not long like a pretzel stick and not a triangular corner pastry. Shown as one whole roll; it must show no seeds, no cheese and no text.

items.name: Seeded Quark Stick
items.desc: A seeded quark stick (Korn-Quark-Stange) is a short, thick wheat roll about 19 cm long and 7 cm wide, made with quark and wound from one twisted strand of dough, so three diagonal spiral seams run around it and its two ends taper to blunt points. The raised bands between the seams are crusted with linseed, sunflower kernels, sesame and poppy seeds, and bare matte golden-brown dough shows inside each seam. It has no lye gloss, no salt and no white cut stripes, unlike the dark pretzel sticks, and it is not round like the seeded rolls. Shown as one whole stick lying diagonally; it must not show cheese and text.

items.name: Potatobrötchen (Potato Roll)
items.desc: A potato roll (Kartoffelbrötchen) is a round rustic roll about 9 cm across, made with potato flakes, with one short straight slash across the top that has opened into a darker ridge. The golden brown crust is dusted with white flour in light patches. It is shown as one whole roll beside a second roll cut in half to show a soft, pale yellow-cream crumb. It has no seeds, no pinwheel pattern and no big white crackle coat, so it is not the Kaiser roll and not the Munich loaf. It must show no text and no packaging.

items.name: Swabian Seele
items.desc: A Seele is a long, thin, hand-pulled Swabian stick about 25 cm long and 5 cm wide, irregular and slightly flattened with uneven ends because the very soft dough spreads in the oven. The crust is thin, crisp and golden brown, and the top is scattered with coarse white salt crystals and brown caraway seeds. It is not glossy dark like a lye stick, has no seed crust like the quark stick, and is flatter and more uneven than a baguette. Shown as one whole stick lying diagonally.

items.name: Simit (Sesame Ring)
items.desc: A simit is a ring-shaped bread about 15 cm across with a hole about 6 cm wide, made from a rope of dough twisted on itself so the ring shows a faint spiral. It is dipped in grape molasses and rolled in sesame, so the whole surface is a dense coat of toasted sesame seeds over a deep reddish golden-brown, crisp crust. It is not a glossy pretzel, not a plain bagel and not a donut. Shown as one whole ring lying flat.

items.name: Red Pepper Baguette
items.desc: A red pepper baguette (Peperonibaguette) is a short baguette about 35 cm long and 7 cm wide with blunt rounded ends. Small diced pieces of sweet red bell pepper are mixed through the dough and show as bright red flecks in the deep golden crust, which carries three shallow diagonal cuts and a light flour dusting. It is shorter and redder than the plain baguette and the stone-oven baguette and has no onion pieces. Shown as one whole loaf lying diagonally; it must not show chili peppers, flames and text.

items.name: Zwiebelbaguette (Onion Baguette)
items.desc: An onion baguette (Zwiebelbaguette) is a short, plump baguette about 22 cm long, pale golden with darker toasted spots, with roasted onion pieces mixed into the dough that show as brown flecks and small crisp bits on the crust. Two diagonal cuts open along the top and the ends are rounded. It has no red pepper flecks, no seeds and no flour dusting. Shown as one whole loaf lying diagonally; it must not show raw onions and text.

items.name: Wheat-Rye Loaf
items.desc: A wheat-rye loaf (Weizenmischbrot) is a free-form oval loaf about 30 cm long, smooth and evenly golden brown, with three shallow diagonal slashes across the top that open into lighter stripes. The crust is thin and slightly shiny with no flour and no crackle; the crumb is fine, soft and light beige. It is an oval, not a round boule with a cross cut and not a straight-sided tin loaf, and it has no seeds. Shown whole with two slices cut and leaning against the end to show the crumb; it must not show text.

items.name: Crusty Round Loaf
items.desc: A wheat crust loaf (Weizenkruste) is a round, domed boule about 20 cm across with a thick, crackly crust in deep golden brown, lightly dusted with white flour. One cross-shaped cut on top has burst open into four raised, paler lobes. The crumb is light and open. It is round, not the oval three-slash wheat-rye loaf and not a straight-sided tin loaf, and it has no seeds. Shown whole with one thick slice cut away and lying in front; it must not show text.

items.name: White Tin Loaf
items.desc: A white tin loaf (Weißbrot) is a rectangular loaf baked in a pan, about 22 cm long and 10 cm wide, with straight, pale, flat sides and a rounded golden top split open lengthwise into one rough, lighter ridge. The crumb is very white, soft and fine. It is the only straight-sided pan loaf of the plain breads, not a free-form oval and not a round boule, and it has no seeds and no flour dusting. Shown whole with two slices cut and lying in front; it must not show a bag and text.

items.name: Rye Mixed Loaf
items.desc: A rye-wheat loaf (Roggenmischbrot, Roggenkruste) is a free-form oval loaf about 28 cm long with a smooth, dull gray-brown dome evenly dusted with a thin veil of white flour, with no cracks, no cuts and no bursts. The crumb is dense, moist and gray-beige. It has no white crackle network like the Mecklenburg loaf, no reddish split like the Siegerland loaf, and no seeds. Shown whole with the end cut off and one slice lying in front; it must not show butter, a board and text.

items.name: Farmhouse Loaf
items.desc: A farmhouse loaf (Bauernbrot) is a free-form oval loaf about 26 cm long with a matte, pale golden-tan, honey-colored crust under a soft even haze of flour; it is not shiny, not glazed and not red. Two deep crosswise cuts have burst wide open into big raised ridges with rough, darker brown torn insides, the clearest mark of this loaf. The crumb is light brown and fairly open. It is paler and more golden than the reddish Siegerland loaf, its flour is an even haze with no flakes and no crackle, and its two wide torn bursts are far deeper than the three thin slashes of the wheat-rye loaf. It has no seeds. Shown whole with two slices cut and lying in front; it must not show text.

items.name: World Champion Loaf
items.desc: A world champion loaf (Weltmeisterbrot) is an oval wheat-rye loaf about 25 cm long whose whole top is densely coated with a speckled mix of white sesame and blue-black poppy seeds over a golden brown crust, with three shallow diagonal cuts. The crumb is light brown and moist. It is not covered in green pumpkin seeds and not a tin loaf. Shown whole with three slices cut and fanned out in front; it must not show text.

items.name: Pumpkin Seed Loaf
items.desc: A pumpkin seed loaf (Kürbiskernbrot) is a rectangular tin loaf about 25 cm long whose whole top is thickly covered with flat, olive-green to toasted-brown pumpkin seeds. The sides are smooth and medium brown, and the crumb is brown, moist and dotted with more pumpkin seeds. It is a tin loaf like the white loaf but dark and seed-crusted, and it has no sesame and no poppy speckle. Shown whole with two slices cut and lying in front; it must not show text.

items.name: Sunflower Seed Loaf
items.desc: A sunflower seed loaf (Sonnenblumenkernbrot) is an oval, dark brown whole-grain loaf about 25 cm long and 500 g whose crust is scattered with pale sunflower kernels and small brown linseeds, slightly crackled and lightly floured. The crumb is dark brown, moist and full of sunflower kernels. It has no green pumpkin seeds, no sesame-poppy coat and no boxy shape. Shown whole with two slices cut from the end.

items.name: Spelt and Emmer Loaf
items.desc: A spelt and emmer loaf (Dinkelbrot mit Emmer) is an oval loaf about 24 cm long and 500 g with a light golden brown crust sprinkled with pale rolled spelt flakes and marked by several shallow diagonal cuts. The crumb is light beige and fairly open. It is lighter than the rye loaves, has no sesame-poppy coat, no pumpkin seeds and no orange carrot flecks. Shown whole with two slices cut from the end.

items.name: Carrot Loaf
items.desc: A carrot loaf (Rüblibrot) is a rectangular tin loaf about 22 cm long with a dark brown, slightly rough top and straight sides. Its dark brown, moist crumb is dotted all through with small bright orange flecks of grated carrot and a few sunflower kernels, which is the one feature that tells it apart, so the cut face must show. It has no seed crust on top, no sesame and no green pumpkin seeds. Shown whole with two slices cut and lying in front to show the orange flecks; it must not show whole carrots and text.

items.name: Mecklenburg Country Loaf
items.desc: A Mecklenburg country loaf is a long free-form oval rye-wheat loaf about 32 cm long whose whole top is thickly coated in white flour that has crazed into a dense network of fine cracks, like dry mud, showing dark brown crust in every crack. It has no cuts and no seeds, and the crumb is gray-brown. Its bright white crackle network over the entire top is its mark; it is not the smooth evenly floured rye-wheat loaf and not the reddish split Siegerland loaf. Shown whole with two slices cut and lying in front; it must not show text.

items.name: Siegerland Country Loaf
items.desc: A Siegerland country loaf is a free-form oval rye-wheat loaf about 30 cm long with a reddish chestnut-brown crust. Flour lies on top in scattered patches that have crackled into small pale flakes, and one long ragged crack runs along one side of the loaf. The crumb is gray-beige, dense and moist. Its reddish crust with patchy flour and one side split is its mark; it is not the dense all-over white crackle of the Mecklenburg loaf and not the smooth gray rye-wheat loaf. Shown whole with the end cut off and one slice lying in front; it must not show text.

items.name: Paderborn Country Loaf
items.desc: A Paderborn country loaf is a large rectangular rye-wheat loaf of about 1 kg, baked packed side by side so it has pale, soft, flat sides and a dome of floury gray-brown crust on top. The crumb is light gray-brown and even. It is block-shaped like a tin loaf but much larger, darker and duller than the white tin loaf, and it has no seed crust. Shown whole with two slices cut from one end.

items.name: Flensburg Dark Rye Loaf
items.desc: A Flensburg dark rye loaf is a free-form oval loaf about 26 cm long with a matte, medium-dark brown crust whose top is finely rough, as if sprinkled with coarse rye meal, with a faint dusting of flour and no cuts. The crumb is brown, dense and moist. It is a plain oval with no seeds, no white crackle network, no reddish split and no glossy bursts. Shown whole with the end cut off and one slice lying in front; it must not show text.

items.name: Munich Small Loaf
items.desc: A Munich small loaf (Münchner Laibchen) is a small round wheat-rye loaf, domed and about 13 cm across, whose whole top is thickly coated in white flour that has burst into wide, irregular cracks showing dark brown crust beneath, like a leopard pattern. It has no cut and no seeds. Its thick white coat split by big dark cracks is its mark; it is not the cross-cut wheat boule, not the curved-slash spelt boule and not the slashed potato roll. Shown as one whole loaf; it must not show slices and text.

items.name: Turkish Flatbread
items.desc: A Turkish flatbread (Fladenbrot) is a round, puffy bread about 20 cm across and only a few centimeters thick, with a soft golden crust whose whole top is scattered with white sesame seeds and some black nigella seeds. The edge is rounded and the inside is white, airy and soft. It is flat and round, unlike every loaf and roll here, and it is not a pizza. Shown whole with one torn piece lying beside it; it must not show fillings and text.

items.name: Spelt Round Loaf
items.desc: A spelt round loaf (Dinkelbrot) is a round boule about 18 cm across with a golden brown crust lightly floured and finely crackled. One long curved slash across the top has opened into a single raised ear with a sharp edge. The crumb is light, open and creamy. It is not the cross-cut wheat boule, not the unscored lumpy Odenwald loaf and not the white-coated Munich loaf, and it has no seeds. Shown whole with two slices cut and lying in front; it must show no stamp, logo, lettering and label.

items.name: Fruit Streusel Danish
items.desc: A fruit streusel danish (Fruchtschnecke) is a round, flat yeast pastry about 11 cm across with a low golden rim. Its top is covered with swirls of bright red fruit filling under scattered pale butter streusel crumbs and thin zigzag lines of white icing. Red fruit plus white icing zigzags is its mark; it is not the apple danish (puffed ring, powdered sugar) and not the plain streusel snail (no fruit, no icing). Shown as one whole pastry from above at a slight angle; it must not show text.

items.name: Cinnamon Franzbrötchen
items.desc: A Franzbrötchen is a Hamburg pastry about 11 cm wide: a slice of rolled, buttery laminated dough pressed flat across the middle, so it splays into a butterfly shape with the spiral layers showing on both sides. Dark brown cinnamon-sugar swirls run through the spirals, and the sugar has caramelized into a shiny, sticky golden-brown surface. It has no icing, no fruit and no nuts. Shown as one whole pastry; it must not show text.

items.name: Hazelnut Swirl
items.desc: A hazelnut swirl (Nussschnecke) is a round spiral yeast pastry about 12 cm across, rolled like a snail shell, with a dark brown hazelnut filling showing clearly as a tight spiral between golden dough layers. The whole top is densely sprinkled with small chopped hazelnut pieces and pale sugar granules. It has no icing lines, no sliced almonds, no red fruit, no streusel crumbs and no apple, and it is not the flat pressed Franzbrötchen. Shown as one whole pastry from above at a slight angle; it must not show text.

items.name: Streusel Snail
items.desc: A streusel snail (Streuselschnecke) is a round, flat yeast pastry about 12 cm across whose rolled spiral of soft golden dough shows clearly at the edges, with the top covered in pale golden butter-crumb streusel. It has no fruit, no icing, no custard and no powdered sugar. The visible dough spiral under plain streusel is its mark; it is not the fruit danish (red fruit, icing zigzags) and not the apple danish (puffed ring, powdered sugar). Shown as one whole pastry from above at a slight angle; it must not show text.

items.name: Apple Streusel Danish
items.desc: An apple streusel danish (Apfelplunder) is a round danish pastry about 12 cm across with a tall, puffed, flaky golden ring around the edge and a center heaped with soft pale apple pieces under golden butter-crumb streusel, dusted with white powdered sugar. The puffed ring and powdered sugar are its mark; it is not the folded triangular apple turnover, not the fruit danish with red fruit and icing, and not the flat streusel snail. Shown as one whole pastry from above at a slight angle; it must not show text.

items.name: Bee Sting Danish
items.desc: A bee sting danish (Bienenstichplunder) is an oblong danish pastry about 14 cm long, folded over a vanilla custard filling that shows as a pale yellow band at the open ends. Its top is covered with a crunchy, glossy layer of sliced almonds baked into golden caramel. It is not a round danish, not a croissant and not a sheet-cake slice. Shown as one whole pastry with a second one cut open beside it to show the custard; it must not show text.

items.name: Vanilla Custard Twist
items.desc: A vanilla custard twist (Vanillestange) is a long danish pastry about 18 cm long and 90 g: a log of yellow vanilla custard wrapped in a spiral of flaky dough strips, so the outside looks like a twisted rope of golden ridges, sprinkled with fine sugar. Pale custard shows at the open ends. It is straight and spiral-wrapped, unlike the folded bee sting danish and the flat pressed Franzbrötchen, and has no almonds. Shown as one whole pastry with a second cut to show the custard.

items.name: Chicken Döner Pocket
items.desc: A chicken döner pocket (Dönertasche) is a folded, half-moon pastry pocket about 16 cm long and 110 g, made of soft wheat dough baked pale golden, with a sealed curved edge and a top sprinkled with seeds and dried herbs. One cut half shows seasoned chicken and sauce inside. It is not a sausage roll (no sausage), not a croissant and not a flat pizza. Shown whole with a second one cut open beside it.

items.name: Rustic Walnut Roll
items.desc: A rustic walnut roll (Walnussbrötchen) is an oblong, squarish roll about 13 cm long with a dark chestnut-brown, crackly crust lightly dusted with white flour. One long lengthwise burst splits the top open, and pieces of brown walnut show inside the burst and in the crust. It has no seed coat on top, so it is not the sunflower, pumpkin, multi-seed and seeded spelt rolls, and it is darker than the stone-oven roll. Shown as one whole roll; it must show no whole walnuts in shells and no text.

items.name: Poppy Seed Butterfly Pastry
items.desc: A poppy seed butterfly pastry (Mohnschmetterling) is a wide, flat, bow-tie-shaped yeast pastry about 13 cm across, made from a filled roll slice cut through the middle and opened flat into two wings. Each wing is a fan of five straight parallel bands running outward from the pinched middle to a scalloped outer edge: wide pale golden dough bands alternating with narrower blue-black poppy seed bands, so golden dough dominates. Many thin white icing threads cross the bands. It has no spirals, no curls and no four separate lobes, and it is not shaped like a drawn butterfly. Shown as one whole pastry from above at a slight angle; it must show no text.

items.name: Lattice Danish with Strawberry Filling
items.desc: A heart lattice danish (Erdbeerromanze) is a heart-shaped yeast pastry about 12 cm across with a smooth golden rim and a center of bright red strawberry filling covered by a crisscross lattice of glossy golden dough strips, so red diamonds show between the strips. It has no streusel, no icing and no fruit pieces on top, which sets it apart from the round fruit streusel danish and the apple danish. Shown as one whole pastry from above at a slight angle; it must show no whole strawberries and no text.

items.name: Laugencroissant (Pretzel Croissant)
items.desc: A pretzel croissant (Laugencroissant) is a plump crescent croissant about 15 cm long, rolled in segments that taper to curved ends, whose whole outside is a glossy, deep reddish-brown pretzel skin from lye. Pale golden flaky layers show in the cracks between the segments. It is crescent-shaped, so it is not the triangular butter pretzel corner and not the oval pretzel roll with a white split, and its lye-brown skin sets it apart from the amber butter croissant. Shown as one whole croissant; it must show no salt crystals, no filling and no text.

items.name: Spelt Bread Wreath
items.desc: A spelt bread ring (Dinkelmais-Kranz) is a round loaf about 20 cm across shaped as a thick wreath with a large hole in the middle. The crust is pale golden brown, heavily dusted with white flour that has crackled into rough patches, with no cuts and no seeds. It is a floury ring, not the sesame-coated simit and not any round loaf without a hole. Shown as one whole ring lying flat at a slight angle; it must show no corn cobs, no paper tag and no text.

items.name: Mustard Crust Loaf
items.desc: A mustard crust loaf (Senfkruste mit Sonnenblumenkernen) is a round boule about 18 cm across with a dark brown, deeply crackled crust whose crown alone is capped with a thick layer of toasted sunflower kernels; the sides are bare. The crumb is gray-brown and moist. Its round shape with a sunflower cap sets it apart from the oval sunflower seed loaf, the green-seeded pumpkin tin loaf and the sesame-poppy world champion loaf. Shown whole with half of it cut away and two slices lying in front; it must show no mustard jar and no text.

items.name: Rye Potato Loaf
items.desc: A rye potato loaf (Kartoffelbrot) is a free-form oval rye-wheat loaf about 28 cm long whose whole crust is coated in a rough layer of pale tan toasted potato flakes, with one long lengthwise slash across the top. The crumb is light gray-beige and soft. The flake coat is its mark: it is not the potato roll, not a white-floured loaf like the Mecklenburg and Munich loaves, and not a seeded loaf. Shown whole with two slices cut and leaning against the end; it must show no potatoes and no text.

items.name: Seeded Country Roll
items.desc: A seeded country roll (Körnerglück) is a round rustic roll about 10 cm across with a golden brown crust scattered with a mix of pale sunflower kernels, green pumpkin seed pieces and golden linseeds, lightly dusted with flour. One deep curved cut runs across the top, and a band of black poppy seeds lines that cut. It is round with a poppy-lined cut, so it is not the oblong sesame-poppy multi-seed roll, not the all-sunflower roll and not the all-pumpkin roll. Shown as one whole roll; it must show no text.

items.name: Curry Sausage Pastry
items.desc: A curry sausage pastry (Currywurst-Snack) is a long, flat puff-pastry log about 16 cm long, golden brown and dusted with reddish curry powder, with three diagonal cuts across the top that show a filling of sliced sausage in red-orange curry ketchup. It is straight and slashed, not the folded half-moon chicken döner pocket and not the sausage roll with a whole sausage peeking out of the ends. Shown as one whole pastry lying diagonally; it must show no fries, no ketchup bottle and no text.

items.name: Rose Roll
items.desc: A rose roll (Rosenbrötchen) is a round rustic wheat roll about 9 cm across, baked seam side up so its top has burst open into four uneven, overlapping torn flaps, like a loosely opened rose. The crust is matte, stone-baked golden brown with a light flour dusting, darker and rougher along the torn edges. It has no center button, no stamped pattern and no symmetric arms, which sets it apart from the Kaiser roll's neat five-arm pinwheel, and it has no seeds. Shown as one whole roll from above at a slight angle; it must show no bag, no label and no text.

items.name: Chocolate Muffin
items.desc: A chocolate muffin is a single tall muffin baked in a plain, unprinted brown pleated paper cup, with a high, dark cocoa-brown domed top that spills slightly over the cup's edge. The top is rough and cracked and studded with melted dark chocolate chunks. It is dark brown all through, with no blueberries, no pale golden crust and no white liner, which sets it apart from the blueberry bakery muffin. Shown from a slight three-quarter side view; it must show no frosting, no cookie pieces, no logo, no wrapper print and no text.

items.name: German Cheesecake
items.desc: A German cheesecake slice (Käsekuchen) is one tall triangular wedge cut from a round cake, with a thin golden shortcrust base and a thick, smooth, pale yellow quark filling under a browned, slightly cracked top. The cut sides are flat and creamy. It has no fruit, no streusel, no glaze and no chocolate, so it is not a sheet-cake piece and not a tray cake. Shown as one wedge standing by itself, with no plate, no fork and no paper under it; it must show no cheese package, no brand name and no text.

items.name: Sheet Cake with Plums
items.desc: A sheet cake with plums (Zwetschgenkuchen) is one rectangular piece cut from a sheet cake, about 10 by 8 cm, with straight cut sides showing a pale golden yeast-dough base. The top is covered with rows of halved, purple-skinned plums standing on edge, their yellow-green flesh glistening with juice. It has no streusel, no custard and no glaze, which sets it apart from the apple streusel and rhubarb strawberry pieces. Shown as one piece by itself, with no plate, no fork and no paper under it; it must show no whole plums and no text.

items.name: Streusel Cake with Apples
items.desc: A streusel cake with apples (Apfel-Streusel-Kuchen) is one square piece cut from a sheet cake, about 9 cm on each side, with straight cut sides showing three layers: a golden base, a layer of soft pale apple pieces and a thick crown of golden butter-crumb streusel. Its square shape with straight cut layers sets it apart from the round apple danish with its puffed ring and powdered sugar. Shown as one piece by itself, with no plate, no fork and no paper under it, turned so a cut side shows; it must show no whole apples and no text.

items.name: Sheet Cake with Rhubarb and Strawberry
items.desc: A sheet cake with rhubarb and strawberry (Rhabarber-Erdbeer-Kuchen) is one rectangular piece cut from a sheet cake, about 10 by 8 cm, with straight cut sides showing a pale golden base and a layer of creamy vanilla custard. The top is covered with chunks of pink-green rhubarb and halved bright red strawberries under a thin clear glaze. It has no streusel and no purple plums. Shown as one piece by itself, with no plate, no fork and no paper under it; it must show no whole rhubarb stalks and no text.

items.name: Marble Cake with Cherries
items.desc: A marble cake with cherries (Kirsch Marmor Kuchen im Schälchen) is a small rectangular cake baked in its own plain, unprinted brown paper baking tray with straight sides. The domed top shows swirls of dark chocolate cake and pale yellow cake, studded with sunken dark red cherries. It is rectangular in a brown tray with a marbled top, unlike the round apple tray cake in its pleated tray. Shown whole in the tray at a slight angle; it must show no glaze, no print on the tray and no text.

items.name: Small Cake with Apple Slices
items.desc: A mini apple cake (Apfelkuchen im Schälchen) is a small round cake baked in its own plain, unprinted, pleated paper tray of natural light-brown baking paper, whose fluted rim stands a little higher than the cake all the way around. The top is covered with fanned thin apple slices arranged in a ring, golden at the edges and shining under a clear apricot glaze, over a pale golden sponge. It is round in a pleated tray with a fan of apple slices, unlike the rectangular marbled cherry cake in its straight-sided tray, and it has no streusel. Shown whole in the tray at a slight angle, the tray filling the frame; it must show no whole apples, no print on the tray and no text.

items.name: Square Raisin Roll
items.desc: A rustic bun with raisins (Rosinenbrötchen) is a squarish, block-shaped wheat roll about 10 cm long with cut, slightly uneven sides and a rough top. The crust is matte and light golden, with no egg wash and no shine, and dark raisins sit in the dough, showing through the crust and at the cut sides. The square cut, matte crust and raisins are its mark: it is not a glossy round bun, not the knotted brioche and not the smooth soft butter roll. Shown as one whole bun standing by itself; it must show no sugar, no icing and no text.

items.name: Alsatian Oval Roll
items.desc: An Alsatian roll (Elsässerbrötchen) is a plump oval roll about 13 cm long with blunt rounded ends. One ragged burst ridge runs lengthwise along the top where the folded seam opened. The crust is matte, golden to chestnut brown and dusted with white flour that has crackled into fine patches. The oval shape with one lengthwise ragged ridge is its mark: it is not the round flour-crackled stone-oven roll, not the round rose roll with torn flaps and not the smooth, shiny split-top roll with a neat cut. Shown as one whole roll lying diagonally; it must show no seeds and no text.

items.name: Odenwald Country Loaf
items.desc: An Odenwald country loaf is a round wheat-rye loaf about 22 cm across baked without any cut, so its whole top has burst into a lumpy, hilly surface of uneven bulges divided by ragged cracks. The crust is crackling and deep golden brown with no flour and no shine. The hilly, uncut top is its mark: it is not the cross-cut wheat boule, not the curved-slash spelt boule and not the glossy two-burst farmhouse loaf, and it has no seeds. Shown as one whole loaf standing by itself; it must show no slices and no text.

items.name: Pull-Apart Party Rolls
items.desc: Pull-apart party rolls (Partysonne) are one large round bake made of eleven small golden rolls baked touching: ten in a ring around one in the center, like a flower. The ring rolls carry toppings in turn: sesame, poppy seed, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds and grated cheese baked golden, and the center roll is plain. Eleven joined rolls in a flower are the mark: it is not a single Kaiser roll and not a single seeded country roll. Shown whole from above at a slight angle, standing by itself; it must show no dips and no text.

items.name: Netzbrot Oval Loaf
items.desc: A Netzbrot wheat loaf is a plump free-form oval loaf about 22 cm long with a medium golden-brown matte crust and darker bare sides. Only the top is strewn with fine short pale flecks, with no cuts and no flour, and the crust has no tiger mosaic, no giraffe pattern and no polygon cells. The crumb is cream-white with small irregular pores. The pale-flecked, uncut top on a golden oval is its mark: it is not the smooth oval wheat-rye loaf with three slashes, not the round cross-cut wheat boule and not the white-floured Munich loaf with big dark cracks. Shown whole with two slices cut and lying in front of it, both slices fully inside the frame; it must show no text.

items.name: Malfabrot Malt Loaf
items.desc: A dark malt loaf (Malfabrot) is a long free-form oval loaf about 30 cm long with a smooth, dark mahogany-brown crust marked by fine shallow cracks, no cuts, no flour and no seeds. The crumb is mid-brown, dense, moist and even, colored by malt. Its smooth dark oval with fine cracks is its mark: it is not the rough rye-meal Flensburg loaf, not the oat-topped malted multigrain tin, not the whole rye tin and not the carrot tin loaf. Shown whole with the end cut off and three slices leaning against it; it must show no text.

items.name: Malted Loaf (Malzmehrkorn)
items.desc: A malted multigrain loaf (Malzmehrkornbrot) is a free-form oval loaf about 26 cm long, baked on the stone and not in a tin, with a dark reddish-brown malt crust. The whole domed top is covered in coarse pale oat and barley flakes, with no flour and no cracks. The crumb is warm brown and dotted with whole grains. Its flake-covered oval sets it apart from the floured, cracked sunflower loaf, the bare smooth dark malt loaf and the flat-topped whole rye tin loaf. Shown whole with two slices cut and leaning at the cut end; it must not show a tin shape, seeds on the sides and text.

items.name: Coarse Rye Tin Loaf
items.desc: A whole rye tin loaf (Roggen-Vollkornbrot) is a rectangular tin loaf about 22 cm long with straight sides and a flat, very dark brown top cracked into a few long lines, with no seeds and no flakes. The cut face shows a dense, almost black-brown crumb packed with whole cracked rye kernels. The kernel-studded crumb in a flat-topped tin is its mark: it has no orange carrot flecks, unlike the carrot tin loaf, and it is not the free-form oval Flensburg loaf. Shown whole with two slices cut and leaning against the end; it must show no text.

items.name: Biokruste Hearth Loaf
items.desc: A dark-baked wheat boule (Weizenbrot) is a round wheat loaf about 20 cm across baked to a deep, almost dark chestnut crust, lightly floured. One deep ragged tear runs across the top and has lifted into a tall overhanging flap of crust. The crumb is creamy and open. The dark bake with one overhanging tear is its mark: it is not the pale straight-sided white tin loaf, not the oval three-slash wheat-rye loaf, not the golden cross-cut boule and not the golden curved-slash spelt boule. Shown as one whole loaf standing by itself; it must show no stamp, no logo and no text.

items.name: Gouda Topped Roll
items.desc: A cheese crust roll (Käsebrötchen) is a flat, diamond-shaped wheat roll about 13 cm long with two pointed ends and a gently domed middle. Its whole top and sides are crusted in a fine, sandy, golden-orange layer of baked grated Gouda crumbs, with no melted cap, no cut and no seeds. The diamond shape coated all over in sandy cheese crumb is its mark: it is not the lye-brown cheese pretzel stick with a melted strip and not the crescent ham and cheese croissant. Shown whole with a second roll torn open to show the soft white crumb; it must show no text.

items.name: Soft Glazed Roll
items.desc: A soft butter roll (Butterbrötchen) is one smooth, oval milk roll about 11 cm long, softly domed, with a perfectly smooth, unbroken, glossy golden top. It has no cut, no stamp pattern, no knot, no seeds and no sugar, and its sides fade to a pale cream where it was baked against its neighbors. The smooth, unbroken glossy top is its mark: it is not the knotted brioche, not the pinwheel Kaiser roll, not the split-top roll with a burst cut and not the joined double roll. Shown as one whole roll standing by itself; it must show no wrapper and no text.

items.name: Alpine Senner Roll
items.desc: An alpine seeded roll (Sennerfladen) is a thick, rectangular wheat-rye roll about 15 cm long, 7 cm wide and 4 cm tall with rounded corners and a flat top. The whole top is crowded with green-gray pumpkin seeds and pale sunflower kernels, with golden shreds of baked Gouda between them. The rectangular block crusted with pumpkin and sunflower seeds is its mark: it is not the round puffy Turkish flatbread, not the squarish all-pumpkin roll and not the diamond cheese crust roll. Shown as one whole roll in a three-quarter view; it must show no tomato topping and no text.

items.name: Seeded Baguette (Mehrkorn)
items.desc: A multigrain baguette (Mehrkornbaguette) is a long, slim baguette about 50 cm long with tapered ends, made from brown grain dough, whose whole crust is coated in a mix of sunflower kernels, sesame, linseed and oat flakes. Five diagonal slashes open along the top into paler ridges. The seed coat on a full-length slashed baguette is its mark: it is not the floury, seedless stone-oven baguette, not the onion-flecked baguette and not the short, uncut seeded quark stick. Shown as one whole baguette lying diagonally; it must show no text.

items.name: Crispy Filled Stick
items.desc: A crispy filled stick (Knusperstange Asia) is a long, slim, straight rolled stick about 20 cm long, a thin crisp wrapper rolled into a tube, golden and coated in fine toasted crumbs. Both ends are open and show a dark savory filling of finely chopped mixed vegetables with orange carrot bits. The open-ended crumb-coated tube with a vegetable filling is its mark: it is not the caraway-salt Seele, not the seed-crusted quark stick and not the glossy seeded pretzel stick. Shown as one whole stick beside a second one cut in half to show the filling; it must show no sauce and no text.

items.name: Poultry Frikandel Roll
items.desc: A poultry sausage pastry (Geflügelrolle) is a straight, round tube of pale golden puff pastry about 15 cm long with six evenly spaced browned bands cut straight across it, each band at right angles to the length. Both ends are open and cut flush, showing a thick, pale beige-pink skinless sausage level with the pastry. The straight crosswise bands with a flush pale sausage are its mark: it is not the spiral-wrapped sausage roll with a red frankfurter sticking out and not the flat slab with diagonal slits and red curry filling. Shown whole with a cut half beside it; it must show no text.
